utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's start. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is the case number, IT-99-36-T, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin and Momir Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Brdjanin, good afternoon to you. Can you hear me in a language that you can understand? THE ACCUSED BRDJANIN: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. I can hear you and I understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. General Talic, can you hear me in a language that you can understand? THE ACCUSED TALIC: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. I can hear you and I understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, Joanna Korner, Julian Nicholls, assisted by Hasan Younis, case manager. Good afternoon, Your Honours, to, as I understand from Mr. Ackerman, the hundredth day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The hundredth day today? I thank you. And good afternoon to you. Appearances for Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. I'm John Ackerman along with Milan Trbojevic and Marela Jevtovic for Mr. Brdjanin. And lest I forget to do this tomorrow, let me advise you today, Your Honours, that Mr. Trbojevic has some duties to perform in Banja Luka next week and will not be with us next week with your permission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I appreciate you telling us that Mr. Ackerman, and Mr. Trbojevic can attend to his other duties in Banja Luka, provided you are going to be here. Appearances for General Talic.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours. I'm Natasha Ivanovic-Fauveau and I represent General Talic. I'd like to apologise on behalf of Slobodan Zecevic who is absent for reasons of health.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And I wish Mr. Zecevic well. So any preliminaries before I raise some matters myself?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, well, it may that -- because I was about to thank Your Honour having heard the arrangement that had been made for tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. That's one matter that I wanted to address.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And tomorrow morning -- tomorrow we will be sitting in the morning and not in the afternoon, starting at 9.00 sharp, and finishing at -- any time between 12.00 and 12.15. I need to be downtown at 12.30 anyway. So -- so that's -- we will be sitting in room 3, Courtroom III, and not here. So that's number one. Number two is -- I'm mainly addressing you, Ms. Korner. But of course, I mean, I would imagine that this will be followed also by the Defence. Between yesterday and today, my personal assistant, legal officer, and myself, we were going through the Sanski Most file, and at a certain point in time I had a few questions which with my legal assistant's help I have clarified to an extent but I require further clarification from you. I'm going to take you back -- I'm sorry I'm surprising you like this, but I'm going to take you back to May of this year when we handed down a decision relating to your motion -- to the Prosecution's motion for admission of certain evidence under the Rule 92 bis statement. I'm going to go through the basics of that decision and what followed afterwards and what still begs some further information. There was a request from the Prosecution for -- to admit under Rule 92 bis the written statements of witnesses 7.12, 7.119, and 7.62. Now, 7.12 actually testified viva voce here. So forget about him. 7.119, on the 8th of July you -- when I say "you," I mean the Prosecution. I'm not in a position to recall whether it was you personally or Mr. Nicholls or Ms. Richterova. I wouldn't -- I wouldn't remember -- or Ms. Sutherland. I wouldn't remember. Anyway, on the 8th of July, we were informed that this witness would testify viva voce in a later stage because of his new job.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that, Your Honour, and I have a feeling that we -- we were probably going to call him sometime this month. I was going to have another look at his statement to see whether we really needed to call him before I made a final decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So we will need to know that --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- for two reasons obviously. First, because if he's going to come here to give evidence viva voce, that automatically kills the Rule 92 bis statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If he's not going to be produced as a viva voce witness, then obviously the -- our decision would --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I understand that, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- will stand.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then there was a question relating to Witness 7.86. Now, we had decided at the time that the decision on whether the written statement of this witness will be admitted or not will be given if and when the Prosecution revives its request to have the written statement of this witness tendered under Rule 92 bis. It sounds complicated, but this is how it was. There was some doubt in our mind when we handed down the decision as to whether you were still asking to have his statement admitted under Rule 92 bis. You had told us that you would consider the -- or reconsider the situation and come back to us. You haven't. So in actual fact, the -- the request as such, as we take it, as I read it, your original request to have the statement of this witness - I repeat, 7.86 - admitted under Rule 92 bis, was left in abeyance upon your own request, and you had promised to come back telling us whether you were reviving this or not. So you will need -- I mean, I don't want obviously an answer from you today, because as I said, I am more or less facing you with all this without having given you prior notice. But I would like you to look into this and then come back at some later point in time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll do that. I've just been given the name of the witness. But it actually rings no bells for me nor do I recall --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I am not mentioning any names for obvious reasons, because I am not in a position to recall whether they are protected or not protected witnesses. I didn't bother to check that. And then we had also decided that the written statements of Witness 7.130 will be admitted on condition that Witness 7.139 -- you remember these were the two sisters.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay? Appears in court to testify viva voce. The Chamber actually does not require 7.130 to attend for cross-examination. When Witness 7.139 appeared in court and testified viva voce on the 20th of June, a question remained in abeyance as to whether the evidence -- or the written statement of 7.130 would be considered or tendered as evidence under Rule 92 bis. We will need a confirmation of that from you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because it seems to be a little bit --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We put it in as corroborative evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And as I understood it, it was Madam Fauveau who had originally, I think agreed -- and I'd have to go back and look at it -- that it could go in provided the other sister testified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. I mean, I would like you to check on this, confirm for me that we can stand by our decision to have this written statement admitted -- yes, Madam Fauveau. Sorry. Thank you. Thank you, Judge. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. We agreed that the statement of Witness 7.130 should be admitted, and I think this statement is already included in the evidence and that it is under number 800-something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I just want to make sure of that. And then we had in our -- Yes, Mr. Ackerman. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have just in front of me here on the screen a Prosecution 92 bis response dated 20 March 2002, which informs Your Honours that they would call 7.12, 7.119, and 7.62 viva voce and would seek to tender 7.86 under 92 bis. Now, whether something changed after that or not, I don't know. But that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. The 7.12, 7.119, 7.62 I have dealt with already myself. 7.86 I have dealt with. I just want a clarification, because it seems to me that the original request to have this witness's statement -- written statement admitted under 92 bis was put in abeyance. So we had the impression that the Prosecution needed to tell us later on whether it wanted -- they wanted to revive the original request or not. And then this is where the problem really lies, and this is why I asked my ALO to sit down and work with me on this. In our decision, we also dealt with witnesses 7.120, 7.146, and 7.51. We had decided at the time that their written statements will be admitted in their current form -- then current form. However, we also required these witnesses to appear for cross-examination. Now, I know that technically speaking the chapter on Sanski Most is not yet concluded; however, I wish to draw your attention, Ms. Korner, that 7.120 has not been brought forward for cross-examination. And the same applies to 7.146. Now, with --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Yes, Your Honour. I'm actually going to have to do a check on --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please. Microphone for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry. I'm going to have to do a check on all of this, and I hope Ms. Sutherland is watching, because she can do the checks while we speak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. It's okay. It's nothing dramatic, but it's -- we're counter-checking and checking everything we came across this, and I wanted to make sure. And then the last witness, and I know that you have an answer to this, was 7.51.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's Mr. Mayhew I'm told.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly, Mr. Mayhew.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm calling him, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So you still intend to --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So our decision with regard to him as far as Rule 92 bis will fall. All right. So that's -- that's all I need. Mostly to tell us whether you are reviving your request --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- re 7.86, and what's the situation with regard to 7.120 and 7.146.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll make sure that we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Take your time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'll tell you tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are not in a hurry. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, while I'm on my feet, I'll just mention one thing: Your Honours would have seen that the next witness when he made the extra statement yesterday referred to a video that he had brought with him, which we've disclosed today. Because it's brand new, it's clearly relevant. But we have no transcript at all. We're hoping for a rush job on some kind of a transcript by the weekend so this witness will certainly go into next week on any showing. And so at the moment I'm leaving in abeyance whether I make an application to play the video until both Defence counsel -- all Defence counsel have had a chance to look at it. If they understand the language, of course. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: On. But I would expect them to reserve their position, not having seen the video in any case. Is that -- is that correct, Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I assume it's the two videos that were handed to us just a few moments ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, it's one of the two. One's the extract that I'm going to play -- oh, no. What's -- sorry -- oh, that's right. Yes, it's one of the two videos that was handed out. One -- the video with the number 4028.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: We'll -- I'll --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So it's not the V000/0800?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, that's the video that was disclosed as Your Honour can see some time ago. We've given -- we've prepared one extract from it on a separate video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. But anyway, we'll come to that later when -- at the appropriate time. There not being any other preliminaries to deal with, the usher perhaps -- usher, we could prepare the room for closed session. I'm sorry with the members of the public, but we will be continuing -- hearing the evidence of a witness we started with yesterday, and there has already been a decision of this Chamber to take the deposition of this witness in closed session. So you will unfortunately not be able to follow at all. My apologies to you, but this is a precautionary measure that we had to take to protect this witness. Thank you. We'll go into closed session, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if Your Honour doesn't mind, then I'll leave Mr. Nicholls to complete the rest of this afternoon's session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, we had hoped to finish with the previous witness in time for you to start giving evidence at least by this time, if not before. Unfortunately things didn't work out as we had hoped and anticipated. We are still not finished with the previous witness, who is required to remain here for at least another half an hour, if not more. At that point in time we have discussed amongst ourselves it's not fair any more to keep you waiting in that room over there. So please do accept the apologies of this Chamber, mine and of the two Judges plus those of everyone concerned here. It's certainly not been done out of disrespect to you. It's a matter over which we had absolutely no control. So I am giving permission for whoever is in charge of you to escort you back to your hotel and -- rather than keep you waiting here, then you would give evidence for five minutes or ten minutes, and we will start with you tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And Your Honour, I think he should -- I'll try and get VWS, but -- that it will be tomorrow morning, and not tomorrow afternoon at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. It will be tomorrow morning and not tomorrow afternoon. Please accept our apologies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we will have a break now and we will resume in 15 minutes' time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: at 6.30 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday the 30th day of August, 2002, at 9.00 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24
